subject.title: Feature request: Auto-send intent/acknowledgment text message before agent processing

question: Should OpenClaw solve this with a core `messages.ackText` config, a generic non-terminal pre-processing hook, or channel-specific placeholder implementations only?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but choosing the permanent config/API boundary changes user-visible defaults, plugin contracts, and channel delivery semantics; automation should not invent that product direction.

options.title: Approve a generic acknowledgement contract
options.body: Add a documented core/plugin API seam that can send one scoped interim acknowledgement and then continue normal model dispatch across capable channels.

options.title: Approve messages.ackText config
options.body: Add a messages-level text acknowledgement config with strict schema, docs, and per-channel/account override semantics, accepting the new config surface.

options.title: Keep channel-specific placeholders only
options.body: Track Slack, Discord, Telegram, and other channel indicators separately and leave this broad cross-channel config request unsolved for now.

recommendation.title: Approve a generic acknowledgement contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented core/plugin API seam that can send one scoped interim acknowledgement and then continue normal model dispatch across capable channels.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits at the reply lifecycle and cross-channel product boundary where recent adjacent ownership and prior review context point most strongly.
